raw_text:
Below is a complete, coach‑friendly 12‑week program you can give your 27‑year‑old beginner client who trains from a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull‑up bar. It integrates the strength phases, week‑by‑week sessions, sets/reps/tempo/RPE guidance, progressions, cardio, Saturday finishers, mobility, recovery and a practical nutrition plan plus equipment recommendations. I’ve written it so you can hand it to the client or use it for remote coaching notes. If you want printable schedules, technique cues for every exercise, or precise calorie/macros for his bodyweight, tell me his weight/height/goal and I’ll calculate.

Quick program overview
- Duration: 12 weeks, split into three 4‑week phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Adaptation — movement quality, volume, work capacity
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength Build — higher intensity, lower reps, added loading
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength Consolidation — heavier progressions, density, testing/deload
- Frequency: 4 primary strength sessions per week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B) + optional cardio and a Saturday “finisher” (fun) session.
- Equipment: yoga mat, doorway pull‑up bar. Recommended purchases: resistance band set, long pull‑up assistance band, 16 kg kettlebell, adjustable dumbbells or backpack/sandbag. See equipment section for details.
- Session length: ~40–60 minutes (incl. warm‑up & cool‑down); finishers 15–30 min.
- Progression: increase reps/sets, move to harder progressions, add tempo eccentric control, add light weight (backpack/kettlebell/dumbbell), reduce assistance for pull‑ups.

Tempo & intensity shorthand
- Tempo format: Eccentric / Pause / Concentric / Pause (e.g., 3/1/1/0). If tempo isn’t specified, use controlled speed with a 2–3s eccentric, moderate concentric.
- RPE guidance: Aim RPE 7–8 for main sets most weeks in Phase 1–2; Phase 2 sets often RPE 7–9 for strength; manage fatigue—if RPE >9 often, back off.
- Rest between sets:
  - Main compound lifts: 60–120s (longer for pull‑up negatives/assisted pull‑ups)
  - Accessory/core: 30–60s

Warm‑up & mobility
- Pre‑session flow (8–10 min): diaphragmatic breathing, cat/cow, world’s greatest stretch, shoulder bandless T‑raises, hip hinge reps, ankle dorsiflexion, glute bridges.
- Post‑session mobility (5–8 min): pick 3–4 stretches (couch stretch, figure‑4, doorway pec stretch, thoracic rotation, calf stretch).
- Dedicated mobility: 15–20 min 1–2×/week or quick 6‑minute mini daily routine.

Nutrition (lean bulk default)
- Small surplus +200–350 kcal/day above maintenance. Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day. Carbs moderate (3–5 g/kg) variable by training day. Fat 20–30% calories. Hydrate 2–3 L/day. Creatine 3–5 g/day recommended. If you want exact calories/macros give weight/goal.

Cardio (2–3×/week recommended)
- LISS 30–40 min on recovery days; HIIT 10–15 min low‑impact intervals 1×/week if desired; short HIIT or circuits after sessions only if not impacting strength performance.
- Keep noisy moves to a minimum if neighbors close.

Equipment recommendations (buy in stages)
- Top priorities: loop resistance bands + long assistance band; adjustable dumbbells or cheap spinlock set; 16 kg kettlebell; backpack for loading. See earlier note for budget tiers.

How progressions happen
- Push: incline → knee → full → elevated → weighted backpack/slow eccentrics.
- Pull: scapular pull → assisted concentric → negative → assisted → strict pull‑ups.
- Squat: box → bodyweight → backpack → single‑leg/pistol.
- Hinge: glute bridge → single‑leg bridge → RDL → loaded RDL.

Testing / tracking
- Log training (sets/reps/RPE), weight weekly, and retest every 4 weeks: max strict pull‑ups, max full push‑ups in one set or in 2 sets, pistol control or single‑leg squats, plank hold. Week 12: deload or test.

Full week templates (applies each week unless otherwise noted)
- Monday — Upper A
- Tuesday — Lower A
- Wednesday — Cardio or Mobility (LISS or rest)
- Thursday — Upper B
- Friday — Cardio / active recovery (HIIT or light LISS)
- Saturday — Lower B + Saturday Finisher (optional same day, short)
- Sunday — Rest or easy mobility/walk

Now the full week‑by‑week program.

PHASE 1 — WEEKS 1–4: ADAPTATION, TECHNIQUE, TOLERANCE
Goal: teach movement patterns, build base strength & control.

Week 1 (foundation)
- Upper A (Mon)
  - Warm‑up 8–10 min (pre‑session flow)
  - Incline push‑ups (hands on countertop): 4×8–12 (tempo 2/0/1/0) RPE 6–7
  - Australian/Inverted rows (low bar or under door bar): 4×6–10 (3/0/1/0) RPE 6–7
  - Dead‑hang + scapular pulls: 3×20–30s hang + 5 scapular pulls
  - Pike hold progression (shoulder prep): 3×20–30s
  - Core: Dead bug 3×10–12 per side
  - Cool‑down mobility 5–8 min
- Lower A (Tue)
  - Warm‑up
  - Glute bridges: 4×10–15 (2/0/1/0)
  - Box/Chair squats: 4×8–12 (3/0/1/0)
  - Slider hamstring curls (towel on smooth floor): 3×6–10
  - Standing calf raises: 3×12–20
  - Side plank: 3×20–40s per side
- Upper B (Thu)
  - Warm‑up
  - Push progression (kneeling or negative full push‑ups): 4×6–10 (3/0/1/0)
  - Pull‑up negatives (jump to top, slow lower 4–6s): 5×3–5 negatives, long rest 90–120s
  - One‑arm row with backpack (support on chair): 3×8–12 each side
  - Floor Y/T raises (for posterior shoulder): 3×12–15
  - Core: Hollow hold 3×15–30s
- Lower B (Sat)
  - Warm‑up
  - Bulgarian split squats (bodyweight): 4×8–10 each leg
  - Single‑leg RDL bodyweight: 3×8–10 each side
  - Slow tempo bodyweight squats: 3×15 (4/0/1/0)
  - Clamshells: 3×15 each side
  - Glute bridge march: 3×10 each side
- Saturday Finisher (fun, optional same day) — pick a short finisher (10–12 min) such as Finisher E (Box‑Style Interval) or a shortened Backpack Grinder; keep RPE moderate.
- Cardio: Wed LISS 20–30 min; Fri optional short HIIT 10 min (low impact).
- Mobility: 6–10 min pre/post and 15‑20 min dedicated session once this week.

Week 2
- Increase sets or reps slightly: add 1 set to main horizontal push/pull (e.g., 5 sets) or add 2 reps per set. Progress incline lower toward knee push‑ups if comfortable. Increase hang time by 5–10s.
- Keep the rest of session structure same.

Week 3
- Push toward full push‑ups on flat where technique allows; increase eccentric tempo to 4s on selected sets.
- For pull work, increase negative duration to 5–6s or begin assisted concentric with a long band looped under knees/feet.
- Add an extra core set if client tolerates volume.

Week 4 (slightly heavier)
- Increase primary set intensity: aim last set close to technical failure but maintain form (RPE 7–8).
- Add 1 more set to main lifts if recovery is good (5 sets for push/pull).
- Record testing numbers (max assisted/unassisted pull‑up reps, full push‑up capacity) for start of Phase 2 comparison.

PHASE 2 — WEEKS 5–8: STRENGTH BUILD
Goal: increase load/intensity; lower reps for strength while preserving technique. Use added load (backpack, kettlebell, dumbbell) as available.

General Phase 2 targets (Push intensity specifics)
- Push exercises target: 4–8 reps per set for main strength work; 4–6 sets where possible.
- Tempo: often 3–1–1–0 (3s eccentric, 1s pause at bottom, explosive concentric) for main sets; for hypertrophy subsets 6–10 reps moderate tempo allowed.
- RPE: Aim 7–9 depending on week — heavier weeks RPE 8–9 for final sets; monitor fatigue. Progress by lowering assistance for pull‑ups, adding backpack load to push‑ups/goblet squats, increasing set count.
- Week‑by‑week progression: Weeks 5–6 increase load/closer progressions; Week 7 add paused reps or short clusters; Week 8 heavy week (add sets or weight) and test.

Week 5
- Upper A (Mon)
  - Warm‑up
  - Full push‑ups: 5×6–8 (3/1/1/0) RPE 7–8. If can't do full, do knees or incline and add eccentric control.
  - Assisted pull‑ups (band or chair): 5×4–6 (3/0/1/0) RPE 7–8
  - Inverted rows feet elevated: 4×6–8
  - Elevated pike push‑ups or pike negatives: 3×6–8
  - Core: T‑press/pallof press with towel loop 3×10–12s each side
- Lower A (Tue)
  - Backpack front load squat (safe front rack hold): 5×6–8
  - Bulgarian split squats: 4×6–8 each leg
  - Single‑leg RDL with backpack: 4×6–8 each side
  - Slider hamstring curl: 3×8–10
  - Plank 3×45–60s
- Upper B (Thu)
  - Warm‑up
  - Decline or diamond push‑ups (choose harder variant): 5×6–8
  - Pull‑up work: attempt small sets unassisted (3 sets of max reps) + assisted sets to reach volume total ~18–24 reps

Thanks — I’ll design a progressive 12‑week strength program tailored to a 27‑year‑old beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull‑up bar. The focus will be foundational strength, movement quality, progressive overload using bodyweight and tempo, and simple recovery and nutrition guidance you can pass to the client. I’ll break the plan into three 4‑week phases (Adaptation → Strength Build → Strength Consolidation), provide week‑by‑week sessions, exercise selection, sets/reps/tempo, progression options, and short notes on warm‑ups, mobility, recovery, and nutrition.

Key assumptions
- Beginner: can’t yet do many strict pull‑ups or pistol squats; can perform basic push‑ups from knees to full as progressions.
- Equipment: yoga mat, doorway pull‑up bar (can be used for hanging, negatives, assisted pull‑ups, rows with feet on floor), household items (backpack) allowed for added load if needed.
- Training frequency: 4 sessions per week (best balance for strength in beginners). Two upper, two lower / full‑body split across the week.
- Each session ≈ 40–60 minutes including warm‑up and cool‑down.

Progression principles
- Increase difficulty by: increasing reps/sets, improving exercise progression (knees → full push‑up), slowing tempo, adding pauses, adding household load (backpack with books), increasing time under tension, reducing assistance, or adding extra set.
- Aim to add small progress every 1–2 weeks.
- Deload built into Phase 3 with a lighter week (Week 12 optional light week) if needed.

General structure per session
- Warm‑up 8–10 min: joint rotations, 2–3 minutes light cardio (marching in place, high knees), dynamic mobility (leg swings, arm circles), movement prep sets at low intensity.
- Main work 25–40 min: 3–6 exercises targeting strength with specified sets/reps/tempo/rest.
- Accessory/core 5–10 min.
- Cool‑down/mobility 5–7 min.

Tempo notation: Eccentric / Pause / Concentric / Pause (for example 3/1/1/0 = 3s down, 1s hold, 1s up)
Rest: 60–120s between sets for main lifts; 30–60s for accessory work.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 — Movement prep & base strength (learning, build tolerance)
Goal: teach technique, establish baseline strength, and build work capacity.

Weekly layout (4 sessions): Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B
Frequency: e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat (or alternate as fits client)

Week 1
Upper A
- Warm‑up
- Horizontal Push: Incline Push‑ups (hands on countertop/sofa) — 4 sets x 8–12 reps, tempo 2/0/1/0, rest 60–90s
- Horizontal Pull: Australian Pull‑ups (in doorway bar low or using table edge; if bar only, do inverted rows with feet on floor under bar) — 4 x 6–10, tempo 3/0/1/0, rest 60–90s
- Vertical Pull: Dead‑hang & Scapular Pulls — 3 x 20–30s hang + 5 scapular pulls
- Overhead Stability: Pike Hold progression — 3 x 20–30s (or pike push‑up negatives if able)
- Core: Dead Bug — 3 x 10–12 each side
Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Hip Hinge: Glute Bridge (single leg assisted if able) — 4 x 10–15, tempo 2/0/1/0
- Squat pattern: Box Squat to chair — 4 x 8–12, tempo 3/0/1/0
- Hamstring: Nordic curl progression (partnerless): Slider hamstring curls (feet on towel on smooth floor) — 3 x 6–10
- Calves: Standing calf raises — 3 x 12–20
- Core: Side plank — 3 x 20–40s per side
Upper B
- Warm‑up
- Push: Kneeling → Full push‑up progression sets (choose level where last 2 reps are challenging): 4 x 6–10, tempo 3/0/1/0
- Pull: Pull‑up negative (jump to top, 4–6s lowering) — 5 x 3–5 negatives, rest 90–120s
- Horizontal Pull: One‑arm row with backpack (supporting hand on chair) — 3 x 8–12 each side
- Shoulders: Bandless face pulls substitute: Y/T raises on floor (lying) — 3 x 12–15
- Core: Hollow hold — 3 x 15–30s
Lower B
- Warm‑up
- Split squat (rear foot on low chair): Bulgarian split squat (bodyweight) — 4 x 8–10 each leg
- Hip hinge: Single‑leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight, hand weight if available) — 3 x 8–10 each side
- Squat: Slow tempo bodyweight squats — 3 x 15 (4/0/1/0)
- Glute control: Clamshells — 3 x 15 each side
- Core: Glute bridge march — 3 x 10 each side

Weeks 2–4 progression
- Week 2: Add 1 set to main push/pull (e.g., 5 sets of push/pull), or increase reps by 1–3; for hangs add hanging time; reduce assistance for push‑ups (lower incline).
- Week 3: Move push progression closer to floor (incline → knee → full); add 1–2s eccentric slowdowns (e.g., 4s down). For pull‑ups, increase negative duration to 5–6s or begin band‑assisted concentric if available (strap a towel for assistance by foot).
- Week 4 (slightly heavier week): Increase sets to 5 for primary lifts, push for last set close to technical failure but maintain form. Track reps and aim to beat them next phase.

PHASE 2: Weeks 5–8 — Strength Build (introduce higher intensity, lower reps)
Goal: Increase strength by shifting to heavier/lower rep ranges via harder progressions, slower tempo on eccentrics, more set volume on main lifts.

Weekly layout remains 4 sessions: Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B

General changes:
- Main compound sets 4–6 sets, reps 4–8 (use harder progressions/added load)
- Add progressive overload options: weighted backpack, slower tempo eccentrics (4–5s), paused reps, more sets.

Week 5
Upper A

- Horizontal Row: Inverted rows feet elevated (use chair) — 4 x 6–8
- Overhead: Pike push‑up negatives or elevated pike push‑ups — 3 x 6–8
- Core: Pallof press variation with towel (isometric anti‑rotation) — 3 x 10–12s each side
Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Squat: Backpack frontloaded squat (safety front rack using backpack) — 5 x 6–8, tempo 3/0/1/0
- Single leg: Bulgarian split squat — 4 x 6–8 each leg
- Hip hinge: Single‑leg Romanian deadlift with backpack — 4 x 6–8 each side
- Hamstring: Slider curl — 3 x 8–10
- Core: Plank — 3 x 45–60s
Upper B
- Warm‑up
- Push: Decline or diamond push‑ups progression depending on strength — 5 x 6–8
- Pull: Pull‑up negatives + attempt eccentrics → 3 x max unassisted pull‑ups across sets (chase 1–3 reps), plus 3 x 6 assisted
- Row: One‑arm backpack row heavier — 4 x 6–8 each
- Shoulders: Lateral raises with backpack modifications (single‑arm carry) — 3 x 10–12
- Core: Hanging knee raises (from bar) or lying leg raises — 3 x 10–12
Lower B
- Warm‑up
- Strength: Pistol squat progression to box (assisted) — 4 x 5–8 each leg
- Hip hinge: Reverse Nordic to glute bridge combo or deep glute bridges weighted — 4 x 6–8
- Calves: Single‑leg calf raises — 4 x 10–15
- Core: RKC plank/ab wheel alternative (slow roll from knees if possible with towel) — 3 x 8–12 controlled reps

Weeks 6–8 progression
- Week 6: Increase load (add more books to backpack), increase eccentric tempos, aim to reduce assistance on pull‑ups by one level.
- Week 7: Replace some reps with paused reps at bottom (1–2s) and try cluster approach for pull‑ups (small sets with short rest).
- Week 8: Heavier week — add set to main lifts (5–6 sets) and aim for best single‑session performance this phase. Test max unassisted pull‑ups attempt (after warm‑up).

PHASE 3: Weeks 9–12 — Strength Consolidation & Specific Overload
Goal: Consolidate strength gains, introduce heavier single‑rep work (where possible), increase density, and prepare for maintenance.

Weekly layout: keep 4 sessions; shift rep ranges partly to 3–6 for main lifts, include one session focused on volume/hypertrophy for recovery.

General approach:
- Two harder sessions (low reps, heavy progressions), two moderate sessions (higher reps, tempo control).
- Add complex set variants: rest‑pause, tempo, isometrics.
- Week 12: taper week or maintenance depending on client fatigue.

Week 9
Upper A (heavy)
- Warm‑up
- Push: Weighted push‑up with backpack (light) or slow tempo full push‑up — 5 x 4–6, tempo 3/1/1/0
- Pull: Pull‑ups (assisted to unassisted): 6 sets x 2–4 reps (work at near max)
- Row: Inverted rows feet elevated — 4 x 6
- Shoulder: Pike push‑ups — 3 x 6–8
- Core: Hanging leg raises — 3 x 8–10
Lower A (volume)
- Warm‑up
- Squat: Backpack squats — 4 x 8–10
- Split squat: Bulgarian — 4 x 8 each
- Hip hinge: Single‑leg RDL — 3 x 8 each
- Hamstrings: Slider curls — 3 x 10–12
- Core: Plank variations with reach — 3 x 45s
Week 10
Upper B (moderate)
- Warm‑up
- Push: Decline push‑ups or diamond — 4 x 8–10
- Pull: Mixed pull work: 3 x 4 slow negatives + 3 x 6 assisted — total volume focus
- Row: One‑arm heavy rows — 4 x 6–8
- Shoulders: Elevated pike push‑up or handstand practice holds — 3 x 15–30s
- Core: T‑holds — 3 x 20–30s
Lower B (heavy)
- Warm‑up
- Pistols/Assisted one‑leg squats — 5 x 4–6 each leg
- Hip hinge: Single‑leg RDL with heavier backpack — 4 x 6 each
- Calves: Elevated single‑leg calf raises — 4 x 12–15
- Core: Heavy anti‑extension (slow rollouts) — 3 x 6–10

Week 11
- Repeat Week 9 but attempt small increases (add 1 rep per main set or add 2–5 kg equivalent by backpack).
- If pull‑up numbers have improved, shift some assisted sets to strict unassisted multiple reps.

Week 12 — Deload / Test
Option A (deload): 60% of week 11 volume and intensity; focus on movement quality, mobility, and recovery.
Option B (test): After proper warm‑up, test 1RM style maximal tests for bodyweight strength:
- Max strict pull‑ups (total reps across sets), max full push‑ups in 2 sets, max pistol attempts, timed plank.
Use whichever fits client energy and stress levels. If they’re fatigued, choose deload.

Goals and how to use cardio with a strength program
- Primary aim: improve aerobic fitness and recovery without compromising strength gains.
- Keep cardio moderate in volume during the strength build phases; do higher volumes only if the client’s goal includes fat loss or endurance.

  - For added fat loss: 3–4 sessions/week (25–40 min) but watch calories and recovery.

Cardio session types (at‑home, small flat)
1) Low‑Intensity Steady State (LISS)
- What: steady rhythmic movement 30–45 min at conversational pace (RPE 4–5 / ~60–70% max HR).
- Examples: brisk marching/jogging on spot, step‑ups on a sturdy step or bottom stair, walking outdoors if possible, easy cycling if they have a bike, steady shadow boxing.
- Why use: low fatigue, promotes recovery and calorie burn; good on rest or active recovery days.
- Progression: increase duration by 5–10 min every 1–2 weeks, or raise pace slightly.

2) High‑Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) — short, intense intervals
- What: repeated high‑effort intervals with rest; 10–20 min total work (excluding warm‑up/cool‑down).
- Examples (all safe in a small flat; reduce impact choices if needed):
  - Tabata style (20s work / 10s rest) × 8 rounds (4 min) — choose bodyweight exercise like squat jumps, mountain climbers, burpees (if floor and noise allow).
  - 30s hard / 30–60s easy × 8–12 rounds — exercises: high knees, jump rope (if space), burpees, tuck jumps, fast bodyweight squat to high knee.
  - EMOM (every minute on the minute): perform 12–15 reps of a hard move, rest remainder of minute, repeat 10–15 min.
- Why use: quick cardio stimulus, time efficient, raises cardiovascular capacity and calorie burn.
- Progression: increase number of rounds, reduce rest, add harder variants (e.g., jump to tuck jump).

Precautions for HIIT in a small flat:
- Impact & neighbors: burpees/jumps can be noisy. Use low‑impact alternatives (fast bodyweight squats, mountain climbers, high‑knees on place without airborne phase).
- Floor/space: ensure mat for cushioning; do hard intervals earlier in day to avoid disturbing others.

3) Circuit Cardio / Metabolic Conditioning
- What: mix cardio moves and strength moves for 15–30 min straight, minimal rest; good for conditioning and calorie burn.
- Example circuit (3–5 rounds):
  - 45s mountain climbers (low impact variation if needed)
  - 45s bodyweight squats
  - 45s plank jacks or mountain climbers
  - 45s alternating reverse lunges
  - 60s rest between rounds
- Why use: blends conditioning and strength endurance; easy to scale.

How to use
- Pre‑workout (warm‑up mobility, 8–10 min): Do the “Pre‑session flow” before each strength session to prime movement.

- Dedicated mobility session (15–20 min): Do on a rest or easy cardio day 1–2× weekly.
- Frequency: Aim for at least 3 sessions/week total; up to daily 10–12 minute mini sessions is fine and beneficial.

General rules & breath
- Move slowly and with control; breathe steadily (inhale on setup, exhale on effort/into deeper position).
- Spend quality time on areas that feel tight or limit technique.
- No bouncing; hold gentle tension at end range 20–60s for positional holds; use 8–12 slow controlled reps for dynamic mobility.
- If a movement causes sharp pain, regress the movement or skip and refer to a professional.

Pre‑session flow (8–10 minutes — before strength sessions)
1) Diaphragmatic breathing & gentle spinal wave — 1–2 minutes
   - Lying on back or seated: 6–8 slow diaphragmatic breaths to calm the nervous system and improve ribcage mobility.
   - Add a gentle cat/cow (on all fours) 6–8 reps to mobilize spine.

2) World’s Greatest Stretch (Thoracic + Hip opener) — 6 reps each side
   - From lunge position, place opposite hand on floor, rotate thorax upward reaching to ceiling, hold 1–2 seconds, return to forward fold; repeat slowly.

3) Shoulder “Bandless” distraction / Doorway T‑raise — 8 reps each side
   - Use towel or long band looped in door frame (low pull if available) or do floor T‑raises: lie face down, arms out in T, lift chest and arms a few cm, squeeze scapulae, 8–12 reps.

4) Hip hinge practice (RDL pattern) — 8–10 reps
   - Slow single‑leg RDL reach (bodyweight) or two‑leg hip hinge: hands slide down shins, hinge from hips keeping neutral spine, 3–4 seconds down, stand up. Focus on glute engagement.

5) Ankle mobility — knee‑to‑wall or half‑kneeling ankle dorsiflexion — 8–10 reps each side
   - Facing a wall, foot close, drive knee forward over toes while keeping heel down; 8–10 reps each ankle. If limited, move foot further from wall.

6) Glute activation (glute bridge march) — 8–10 reps each leg
   - Lying on back, bridge to hip extension then alternate marching with control; pause at top to feel glutes.

Post‑session (5–8 minutes — after workouts)
Pick 3–4 of the following to address the session’s focus; hold each 20–45s or perform 8–12 slow reps.

1) Couch stretch (quads & hip flexors)
   - One knee on mat, other foot in front, hips square. Lean forward to feel front thigh/hip flexor stretch. Hold 30–45s each side. If no couch, use wall/sofa edge.

2) Figure‑4 glute stretch (supine)
   - Lying on back, cross ankle over opposite thigh and pull the uncrossed thigh toward chest. Hold 30s each side.

3) Doorway pec stretch (chest)
   - Place forearm on doorframe at ~90° and rotate body away to stretch pec and anterior shoulder. Hold 20–30s each side.

4) Kneeling thoracic rotation / thread the needle (on all fours)
   - Reach one arm under body and rotate open toward ceiling. 8–10 slow reps each side or hold end position 20–30s.

5) Seated hamstring single‑leg stretch (active)
   - Straighten one leg, hinge from hips keeping spine neutral and reach toward toes slowly. Hold 20–30s.

6) Calf stretch against wall
   - Straight leg with heel down, lean forward to feel stretch. 30s each side.

  - Lay on a rolled towel or tennis ball along upper back and gently move to find tight spots (avoid spine).

Below is a complete, coach‑friendly 12‑week program you can give your 27‑year‑old beginner client who trains from a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull‑up bar. It integrates the strength phases, week‑by‑week sessions, sets/reps/tempo/RPE guidance, progressions, cardio, Saturday finishers, mobility, recovery and a practical nutrition plan plus equipment recommendations. I’ve written it so you can hand it to the client or use it for remote coaching notes. If you want printable schedules, technique cues for every exercise, or precise calorie/macros for his bodyweight, tell me his weight/height/goal and I’ll calculate.

Quick program overview
- Duration: 12 weeks, split into three 4‑week phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Adaptation — movement quality, volume, work capacity
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength Build — higher intensity, lower reps, added loading
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength Consolidation — heavier progressions, density, testing/deload
- Frequency: 4 primary strength sessions per week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B) + optional cardio and a Saturday “finisher” (fun) session.
- Equipment: yoga mat, doorway pull‑up bar. Recommended purchases: resistance band set, long pull‑up assistance band, 16 kg kettlebell, adjustable dumbbells or backpack/sandbag. See equipment section for details.
- Session length: ~40–60 minutes (incl. warm‑up & cool‑down); finishers 15–30 min.
- Progression: increase reps/sets, move to harder progressions, add tempo eccentric control, add light weight (backpack/kettlebell/dumbbell), reduce assistance for pull‑ups.

Tempo & intensity shorthand
- Tempo format: Eccentric / Pause / Concentric / Pause (e.g., 3/1/1/0). If tempo isn’t specified, use controlled speed with a 2–3s eccentric, moderate concentric.
- RPE guidance: Aim RPE 7–8 for main sets most weeks in Phase 1–2; Phase 2 sets often RPE 7–9 for strength; manage fatigue—if RPE >9 often, back off.
- Rest between sets:
  - Main compound lifts: 60–120s (longer for pull‑up negatives/assisted pull‑ups)
  - Accessory/core: 30–60s

Warm‑up & mobility
- Pre‑session flow (8–10 min): diaphragmatic breathing, cat/cow, world’s greatest stretch, shoulder bandless T‑raises, hip hinge reps, ankle dorsiflexion, glute bridges.
- Post‑session mobility (5–8 min): pick 3–4 stretches (couch stretch, figure‑4, doorway pec stretch, thoracic rotation, calf stretch).
- Dedicated mobility: 15–20 min 1–2×/week or quick 6‑minute mini daily routine.

Nutrition (lean bulk default)
- Small surplus +200–350 kcal/day above maintenance. Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day. Carbs moderate (3–5 g/kg) variable by training day. Fat 20–30% calories. Hydrate 2–3 L/day. Creatine 3–5 g/day recommended. If you want exact calories/macros give weight/goal.

Cardio (2–3×/week recommended)
- LISS 30–40 min on recovery days; HIIT 10–15 min low‑impact intervals 1×/week if desired; short HIIT or circuits after sessions only if not impacting strength performance.
- Keep noisy moves to a minimum if neighbors close.

Equipment recommendations (buy in stages)
- Top priorities: loop resistance bands + long assistance band; adjustable dumbbells or cheap spinlock set; 16 kg kettlebell; backpack for loading. See earlier note for budget tiers.

How progressions happen
- Push: incline → knee → full → elevated → weighted backpack/slow eccentrics.
- Pull: scapular pull → assisted concentric → negative → assisted → strict pull‑ups.
- Squat: box → bodyweight → backpack → single‑leg/pistol.
- Hinge: glute bridge → single‑leg bridge → RDL → loaded RDL.

Testing / tracking
- Log training (sets/reps/RPE), weight weekly, and retest every 4 weeks: max strict pull‑ups, max full push‑ups in one set or in 2 sets, pistol control or single‑leg squats, plank hold. Week 12: deload or test.

- Tuesday — Lower A
- Wednesday — Cardio or Mobility (LISS or rest)
- Thursday — Upper B
- Friday — Cardio / active recovery (HIIT or light LISS)

PHASE 1 — WEEKS 1–4: ADAPTATION, TECHNIQUE, TOLERANCE
Goal: teach movement patterns, build base strength & control.

Week 1 (foundation)
- Upper A (Mon)
  - Warm‑up 8–10 min (pre‑session flow)
  - Incline push‑ups (hands on countertop): 4×8–12 (tempo 2/0/1/0) RPE 6–7
  - Australian/Inverted rows (low bar or under door bar): 4×6–10 (3/0/1/0) RPE 6–7
  - Dead‑hang + scapular pulls: 3×20–30s hang + 5 scapular pulls
  - Pike hold progression (shoulder prep): 3×20–30s
  - Core: Dead bug 3×10–12 per side
  - Cool‑down mobility 5–8 min
- Lower A (Tue)
  - Warm‑up
  - Glute bridges: 4×10–15 (2/0/1/0)
  - Box/Chair squats: 4×8–12 (3/0/1/0)
  - Slider hamstring curls (towel on smooth floor): 3×6–10
  - Standing calf raises: 3×12–20
  - Side plank: 3×20–40s per side
- Upper B (Thu)
  - Warm‑up
  - Push progression (kneeling or negative full push‑ups): 4×6–10 (3/0/1/0)
  - Pull‑up negatives (jump to top, slow lower 4–6s): 5×3–5 negatives, long rest 90–120s
  - One‑arm row with backpack (support on chair): 3×8–12 each side
  - Floor Y/T raises (for posterior shoulder): 3×12–15
  - Core: Hollow hold 3×15–30s
- Lower B (Sat)
  - Warm‑up
  - Bulgarian split squats (bodyweight): 4×8–10 each leg
  - Single‑leg RDL bodyweight: 3×8–10 each side
  - Slow tempo bodyweight squats: 3×15 (4/0/1/0)
  - Clamshells: 3×15 each side
  - Glute bridge march: 3×10 each side
- Saturday Finisher (fun, optional same day) — pick a short finisher (10–12 min) such as Finisher E (Box‑Style Interval) or a shortened Backpack Grinder; keep RPE moderate.
- Cardio: Wed LISS 20–30 min; Fri optional short HIIT 10 min (low impact).
- Mobility: 6–10 min pre/post and 15‑20 min dedicated session once this week.

Week 2
- Increase sets or reps slightly: add 1 set to main horizontal push/pull (e.g., 5 sets) or add 2 reps per set. Progress incline lower toward knee push‑ups if comfortable. Increase hang time by 5–10s.
- Keep the rest of session structure same.

Week 3
- Push toward full push‑ups on flat where technique allows; increase eccentric tempo to 4s on selected sets.
- For pull work, increase negative duration to 5–6s or begin assisted concentric with a long band looped under knees/feet.
- Add an extra core set if client tolerates volume.

Week 4 (slightly heavier)
- Increase primary set intensity: aim last set close to technical failure but maintain form (RPE 7–8).
- Add 1 more set to main lifts if recovery is good (5 sets for push/pull).
- Record testing numbers (max assisted/unassisted pull‑up reps, full push‑up capacity) for start of Phase 2 comparison.

PHASE 2 — WEEKS 5–8: STRENGTH BUILD
Goal: increase load/intensity; lower reps for strength while preserving technique. Use added load (backpack, kettlebell, dumbbell) as available.

General Phase 2 targets (Push intensity specifics)
- Push exercises target: 4–8 reps per set for main strength work; 4–6 sets where possible.
- Tempo: often 3–1–1–0 (3s eccentric, 1s pause at bottom, explosive concentric) for main sets; for hypertrophy subsets 6–10 reps moderate tempo allowed.
- RPE: Aim 7–9 depending on week — heavier weeks RPE 8–9 for final sets; monitor fatigue. Progress by lowering assistance for pull‑ups, adding backpack load to push‑ups/goblet squats, increasing set count.
- Week‑by‑week progression: Weeks 5–6 increase load/closer progressions; Week 7 add paused reps or short clusters; Week 8 heavy week (add sets or weight) and test.

Week 5
- Upper A (Mon)
  - Warm‑up
  - Full push‑ups: 5×6–8 (3/1/1/0) RPE 7–8. If can't do full, do knees or incline and add eccentric control.
  - Assisted pull‑ups (band or chair): 5×4–6 (3/0/1/0) RPE 7–8
  - Inverted rows feet elevated: 4×6–8
  - Elevated pike push‑ups or pike negatives: 3×6–8
  - Core: T‑press/pallof press with towel loop 3×10–12s each side
- Lower A (Tue)
  - Backpack front load squat (safe front rack hold): 5×6–8
  - Bulgarian split squats: 4×6–8 each leg
  - Single‑leg RDL with backpack: 4×6–8 each side
  - Slider hamstring curl: 3×8–10
  - Plank 3×45–60s
- Upper B (Thu)
  - Warm‑up
  - Decline or diamond push‑ups (choose harder variant): 5×6–8
  - Pull‑up work: attempt small sets unassisted (3 sets of max reps) + assisted sets to reach volume total ~18–24 reps
  - One‑arm backpack row heavy: 4×6–8 each side
  - Floor lateral raise / Y/T: 3×12–15
  - Hanging knee raises or lying leg raises: 3×10–12
- Lower B (Sat)
  - Warm‑up
  - Pistol progressions to box (assisted): 4×5–8 each leg
  - Reverse Nordic / glute‑bridge combo: 4×6–8
  - Single‑leg calf raises: 4×10–15
  - Ab wheel alternative (slow rollouts with towel): 3×8–12
- Saturday Finisher: pick from Finisher A–E. Moderate intensity (RPE 6–7).
- Cardio: Wed LISS 30 min; Fri optional HIIT 12 min low‑impact.
- Mobility: pre/post and one 15–20 min session that week.

Week 6
- Increase load slightly: add weight to backpack (1–3 kg) or increase kettlebell/dumbbell weight if available. For push sets, maintain 5 sets of 6–8 but aim to increase reps or reduce assistance on pull‑ups.
- Option: add eccentric emphasis on 1–2 sets per push exercise (4–5s down).
- Keep rest 90s on pull‑up sets.

Week 7
- Add small intensity variations: paused reps at bottom for push‑ups (1–2s), cluster sets for pull‑ups (e.g., 3×2 with 20s rest x 3 clusters), or increase sets to 6 for main lifts if recovery good.
- Emphasize reducing assistance for pull‑ups by 1 level (thinner band or more foot involvement).

Week 8 (heavier week / test)
- Heavier week: aim for 5–6 sets of main lifts with rep range 4–6 for strength focus.
- Test progress: see if unassisted pull‑ups increased, push‑ups per set increased. Capture metrics for Phase 3 planning.
- Ensure recovery: good sleep and nutrition.

PHASE 3 — WEEKS 9–12: CONSOLIDATION, DENSITY, DELoad/TEST
Goal: consolidate strength gains, add density/volume, and provide a deload or test in Week 12.

General notes
- Two sessions per week heavier (low rep, high intensity); two moderate sessions (higher reps/volume). Maintain technique priorities.
- Continue progressive loading (dumbbells/kettlebells/backpack) and reduce assistance on pull‑ups.

Week 9
- Upper A (Mon – heavy)
  - Warm‑up
  - Weighted (backpack) push‑ups or slow tempo full push‑ups: 5×4–6 (3/1/1/0) RPE 8
  - Pull‑ups: 6 sets × 2–4 reps (work near max; use assistance only to finish reps)
  - Inverted rows feet elevated: 4×6
  - Pike push‑ups: 3×6–8
  - Hanging leg raises: 3×8–10
- Lower A (Tue – volume)
  - Backpack squats: 4×8–10
  - Bulgarian split squats: 4×8 each
  - Single‑leg RDL: 3×8 each
  - Slider curls 3×10–12
  - Plank variations 3×45s
- Upper B (Thu – moderate)
  - Decline/diamond push‑ups: 4×8–10
  - Mixed pull set: 3×4 slow negatives + 3×6 assisted
  - One‑arm heavy rows: 4×6–8 each
  - Pike/handstand practice holds 3×15–30s
  - Core: T‑holds 3×20–30s
- Lower B (Sat – heavy)
  - Pistol/assisted pistols: 5×4–6 each leg
  - Single‑leg RDL with heavier weight: 4×6 each
  - Calves: elevated single‑leg 4×12–15
  - Core: slow rollouts 3×6–10
- Saturday Finisher: choose one; can be higher intensity this phase (Finisher A or B) but limit to RPE 7–8.
- Cardio: Wed LISS 30 min; Fri optional HIIT 12–15 min.
- Mobility: maintain pre/post flow and 15–20 min session weekly.

Week 10
- Similar to Week 9 but swap heavy and moderate emphasis on upper sessions if desired for variety.
- Aim to add small increments in backpack or reps for main lifts.

Week 11
- Repeat Week 9 with small increases: add 1 rep per set on main lifts or add ~2–3 kg equivalent load in backpack/kettlebell/dumbbell where safe.
- Shift assisted pull‑up sets into more unassisted sets if able.

Week 12 — Deload or Test week (coach’s choice)
- Option A — Deload (recommended if fatigue high):
  - Reduce volume and intensity to ~60% of Week 11. Keep movement quality. Shorter sessions, light loads, mobility focus.
  - Cardio reduced to light LISS 20–30 min only.
  - Saturday finisher: light mobility or a very short fun finisher (low intensity).
- Option B — Test week:
  - After full warm‑up, test:
    - Max unassisted strict pull‑ups (total reps),
    - Max full push‑ups in a single set (or two sets with short rest),
    - Single‑leg squat / pistol depth control (quality repetitions),
    - Plank hold max time.
  - Keep other sessions light and mobility focused to avoid injury before tests.
- Record results and plan next training block based on goals and equipment acquired.
